messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I want my fair financial share, and I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. B’s needs matter too. I don’t want to hurt my twin, but that doesn’t mean I’ve agreed. Your wording fits; “taken seriously” sounds more direct than “worth caring about.”

Thank you. My husband and I are interested because owning the house would help me build financial independence. I’d want my sisters to know I’m not treating it as settled; C hasn’t agreed, and the price and terms aren’t decided. Your wording fits—being taken seriously doesn’t mean everyone has to agree.

Thank you. What matters to me is having some money to start a dance studio; that’s what I’d use it for. I’m not sure what I want about the house or the will yet, and I’d rather not settle anything before everyone’s concerns are heard. Your wording fits for me. I don’t have anything else to share just now.

C1 fits: I want a fair share, not to subsidize A’s discounted purchase. C2 fits: B’s needs should be considered too; that doesn’t decide anyone’s share. C3 fits—I care about A and don’t want to hurt her, but I need to be honest. C4 fits: my agreement is mine to give or withhold. M1, M2, and M3 all fit.

A1, A2, A3, A4, and A5 fit. Independence matters to me because I want more security of my own; clarity, genuine agreement, and open terms matter because nothing is settled. Being taken seriously doesn’t require agreement. M1 fits, and M3 fits too: the list should stay open to correction.
B1, B2, and B3 fit for me. M3 fits too. M1 fits for me, though I can’t speak for my sisters. I’d rather leave anything else out for now.

M1–M3 fit. Option 1 is fine as a no-commitment first step. Option 2 is only acceptable if there’s no assumed discount and my fair share is determined under the will with proper advice; I’m not agreeing to a purchase. I’m uneasy about Option 3’s “set period”—there’s no real deadline, and I’m not in a hurry. None settles C1 yet.

Options 1 and 3 feel okay as processes, but neither advances A1 by itself; they do keep the purchase possibility open and fit A2–A5 and M1–M3. Option 2 could fit too, provided a discount can still be discussed rather than ruled out—I want one, but don’t assume I’m entitled to it. I have no other discomfort with the list. Costs, timing, and terms remain unresolved.

Option 1 feels comfortable and fits B2–B3 and M1–M3, though it doesn’t yet give me a real opportunity for the studio. Option 2 could be considered, but it doesn’t guarantee that either, and I’d want no pressure to accept. Option 3 mostly fits, but a set pause period could feel pressuring depending on the timing. I’m not ready to choose between them; that can stay unresolved.

No real deadline means there’s no reason to rush into terms I don’t accept. I’m not in a hurry; I want this handled fairly, not under pressure. C1 should stay unresolved for now—I’m not asking anyone to produce an outcome. C5 and M4 fit.
